acceptance.acceptance_criterion: The same register/edit/validate/plan/submit/query commands work headlessly and through HTTP with identical semantic results and errors, without a synthetic request or private imports
acceptance.observed_result: The 18-test managed-application suite passed. Headless and HTTP registration/edit/validation/plan/submit paths produced matching semantic results; validation metadata, plan fingerprints and snapshots matched. Status, action discovery and resumable event history matched on the same managed service. Pending report/lineage/artifact and missing-definition reads returned the same status and error codes. The test found and fixed omitted headless validation metadata and the run-action schema identifier. A clean Python 3.14.3 wheel install repeated validation, action and event parity and idempotent receipt recovery.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Per-operation authorization precedes lookup; explicit disclosure policy, cross-tenant/workspace/owner isolation and concurrent calls are equivalent across adapters
acceptance.observed_result: All 89 protected CP operations among 91 public OpenAPI operations passed a dynamic authorization-order campaign. Authorization trace preceded every configured store call; denied definition requests performed no repository access, and run existence probes occurred only after authorization. Concurrent headless and HTTP calls for seeded runs preserved explicit opaque not_found (404) and forbidden (403) decisions with matching error codes and no existence probes. The existing tenant/workspace API matrix plus owner, tenant and workspace input-resource attacks produced matching opaque 404 outcomes through headless store and HTTP paths; the owner upload remained intact. The campaign exposed and fixed register/edit endpoints that returned 501 before authorization when managed services were absent. The combined focused authz, managed parity and core disclosure suites passed 103 tests.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Configuration constructs a standard backend; explicit resource ownership, shared lifespans, partial-start cleanup and shutdown preserve accepted durable work
acceptance.observed_result: The managed configuration constructs the SQLModel backend over the explicitly migrated schema. Local lifecycle tests verified partial initialization and startup failures dispose the engine, shutdown disposes the app-owned pool, and accepted durable work remains queryable after a new backend opens the same SQLite database (4 tests passed).

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Every qualified public field, command and query has a coverage-map row through storage to runtime; omitted/downgraded controls fail qualification
acceptance.observed_result: The generated CP public-control inventory covers all 96 OpenAPI operations and 978 path/query parameter and request/response schema fields. Managed schedule request properties now expose revision policy, versioned parameter/secret references, and workload identity instead of disappearing inside an untyped body. Each operation maps to its storage authority and runtime consumer, or an explicit no-ETL-runtime reason. The drift gate validates source/test anchors and rejects an omitted operation, downgraded control, or removed field; all five focused tests passed.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Typed request import/export preserves overrides and extension data; defaults/precedence and effective-setting provenance are deterministic and inspectable
acceptance.observed_result: Typed request import/export preserves overrides and strict, namespaced extension data. Tests cover alias isolation, unknown semantics, profile precedence, explicitly selected default values, and deterministic provenance. Execution-envelope /2 stores both requested and resolved requests; the managed worker consumes the resolved request. Legacy /1 envelopes upgrade using historical default precedence. The focused runtime tests passed (20), managed HTTP/runtime suites passed (281), and a clean wheel installation passed the request and envelope schema smoke check.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Installed-provider discovery supplies schemas, types, constraints, defaults, sensitivity and compatibility; unknown semantic options are rejected with a stable reason
acceptance.observed_result: Profile-authorized installed-provider discovery returns connector JSON Schema, field types, defaults and constraints, protocol and package versions, capabilities and maturity; unsupported options fail planning with stable PMCONN880 without echoing submitted values. The versioned catalog is shared by headless and HTTP callers and requires authorization before discovery. It marks secret-like options, removes defaults/examples/enums from sensitive fields, and recursively removes credential-named members from nested samples. The 69-case catalog/schema/discovery suite and final 6-case privacy/parity/authz/OpenAPI rerun passed; the clean wheel smoke resolved Foundry source/sink/storage schemas, package versions, the catalog contract, and the built-in local-files provider.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: One command resolves revisions/resources and derives plan/effective fingerprints; forged hashes/revisions cannot bypass planning, policy or approval binding
acceptance.observed_result: Managed submit resolves the exact definition revision, validates and verifies the final plan, authorizes each referenced logical resource and finalized input, derives plugin/resource versions and computes the effective fingerprint before policy, approval, quota, and durable acceptance. The captured policy decision binds the effective fingerprint and resolved revision. A matching independent approval admits the request; the same approval cannot authorize a changed revision. Forged plan hashes and unknown revision selectors are rejected without durable acceptance. Finalized owner-bound input versions are recorded in the execution envelope and leased through retry/rerun/replay retention. Exact pinned/latest-approved revision and idempotent retry behavior are covered; AC056-002 supplies the completed cross-scope authorization/disclosure matrix. The managed application plus immutable-input regression run passed 21 tests.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Identical scoped retries recover the same receipt before live work or quota charging; changed intent conflicts, including concurrent requests
acceptance.observed_result: Eight independent processes submitted the same pinned run through separate managed-service instances; all recovered one receipt, the durable outbox contained one command, the persisted concurrency quota was charged once, and a reopened service recovered the receipt. A concurrent two-intent race returned one accepted receipt to four matching callers and conflicts to the four changed-intent callers. PostgreSQL 16.13 multiprocess store tests also verified same-intent acceptance, changed-intent conflict, quota idempotency, restart reads, and recovery after a committed acceptance acknowledgement was lost.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Long preparation survives process death and supports query/cancel by operation ID, without app-side sequencing or secret exposure
acceptance.observed_result: The 66-test managed-preparation, action-job, authorization, coverage and OpenAPI campaign passed. A SQLModel-backed managed API persisted a preparation by operation ID; after the backend closed with the operation claimed and its lease expired, a new backend queried the same operation, took over under a new fence and completed exactly one managed submission and outbox command. Idempotency replay returned the same operation. The SQL-backed API canceled a queued operation and rejected secret-like request content before persistence. Memory integration canceled a running preparation before acceptance and verified no run submission or outbox command was created. A 1.5-second preparation under a one-second lease renewed its lease so a competing worker could not claim it. The SQLModel restart recovery test also verified action-job persistence across engine disposal/reopen and a new attempt/fencing token.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Failure at every CP1/CP3/outbox boundary leaves a discoverable accepted command or a recoverable, explicit rejection; no orphan or duplicate execution
acceptance.observed_result: CP1 and CP3 acceptance reconcile lost commit acknowledgements by the scoped idempotency key. Tests cover pre-commit CP1 rejection, CP1 commit with acknowledgement loss, temporary CP1 reconciliation-read failure and retry, CP3 definite rejection, CP3 commit with acknowledgement loss, temporary CP3 reconciliation-read failure and retry, and PostgreSQL failure inserting the normalized outbox row. The PostgreSQL transaction rolled back the durable snapshot/submission/outbox together while preserving the discoverable CP1 receipt; a new backend instance recovered the same command and published exactly one outbox record. The recovered in-memory command executed once and a same-key replay created no second execution. Six focused managed boundary cases and the 27-test managed application suite passed; the PostgreSQL durable/multiprocess and managed process campaign passed 7 tests.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Static checks remain pure; live preflight uses bounded executors; policy, approvals, quotas and evidence freshness are checked against the final effective plan
acceptance.observed_result: A 55-test admission/preflight campaign passed. Static validate/plan tests prove source reads and transformations are not invoked. The bounded action worker cancels a live handler at its deadline. Managed policy and approvals use the resolved effective fingerprint and immutable revision; concurrency tests confirm same-intent quota admission is charged once. Plan-attestation signatures now bind created_at, freshness verification rejects stale/future or timezone-naive evidence, and pre-submit checks bind the attestation to the effective fingerprint before quota admission. Focused control-plane, HTTP-attestation, managed-submission, action-worker, ruff, and Pyright checks passed.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: A packaged worker performs real ETL from a submitted canonical definition without a caller runner; missing execution support fails closed
acceptance.observed_result: The standard SQLModel backend creates a worker with the packaged runtime adapter. A clean install of the core, FastAPI and SQLModel wheels on Python 3.14.3 migrated to 007 and transferred a canonical JSON-to-CSV definition without a caller runner. The host rejects a runner that returns no typed runtime report rather than reporting a successful ETL run.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Long work renews leases, reacts to in-flight cancellation and fences stale owners; advertised row/byte/time/memory/concurrency limits are enforced
acceptance.observed_result: A targeted lease/fencing/resource campaign passed 86 tests. The broader runtime/resource campaign passed 329 tests with 3 optional skips. Run and preparation workers renewed leases during long work; a competing run worker could not take over before the renewed lease expired. Running cancellation stopped the managed runtime before its sink write, durable state retained unknown effect until reconciliation, and stale fencing tokens could not advance checkpoints. The preparation worker now records deadline expiry as timed_out after cooperative cancellation checkpoints. Row, byte and cooperative time bounds were exercised by storage, local file, inference and Parquet campaigns; local profile concurrency stayed at its configured cap and adaptive invalid concurrency failed before storage effects. DuckDB applied and reported the configured 16 MiB memory limit, while an invalid limit failed before publishing a session. Execution, scheduler and action worker constructors reject boolean, nonpositive, floating-point and missing lease TTLs; the managed action lease is required to exceed the maximum preparation deadline.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Crash after outbox publication, lease expiry, worker death and restart recover safely with stable attempt identities
acceptance.observed_result: The standard SQLModel backend worker completed a real transfer, then a fault injected at the attempt-finalization boundary simulated worker death after report publication. After the one-second lease expired and the backend reopened, the worker reconciled the stored report without reading changed source contents or writing the sink again. The durable report kept both distinct attempt IDs with executed/result_reconciled roles, and start/completion events linked each attempt to the same submission and run.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Unknown commits, lost acknowledgements and partial multi-sink effects require reconciliation; no automatic duplicate write or invented rollback
acceptance.observed_result: Managed retry/rerun tests keep unresolved execution effects blocked before new outbox acceptance. A two-sink runtime campaign deliberately publishes the first sink and fails the second: the first sink remains visible without a fabricated rollback, the run is not successful, and both cursors remain at their previous committed values. Semblance lost-commit acknowledgements reconcile to the already committed transaction; a lost transaction-create acknowledgement remains unknown and is not claimed committed. The isolated PostgreSQL live-provider campaign injected a lost commit acknowledgement, then reconciled the committed effect by querying provider state; failed staging rolled back. Eight simulator/managed/runtime tests and one PostgreSQL test passed.
provider_version_tuple: Semblance 0.9.0 loopback simulator; PostgreSQL 16.14 isolated loopback; ETLantic workspace candidate

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Checkpoint/cursor advancement follows durable publication semantics; cleanup/drain/interruption are idempotent, scoped and observable
acceptance.observed_result: The cursor, result-retention, scheduler-loop, and native interruption campaigns passed. Two-sink incremental success stages both candidates and commits both cursors only after all selected outputs publish; a second-sink failure leaves both committed cursors untouched. Memory batches validate fully before mutation. FileStateStore performs one locked atomic read-modify-write for the full cursor batch and the values survive reopening. Result-retention tests cover bounded retry, scope isolation and restart; scheduler drain stops polling; native cancellation tests prove owned work drains and stale output is not published. The packaged adaptive physical-candidate suite was invoked but its 53 cases were skipped because that candidate is not qualified for this ETLantic version; those skips are not counted as passing physical-executor evidence.
provider_version_tuple: ETLantic workspace candidate; memory and safe file-backed state stores

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Public status/report/lineage/artifacts reflect actual runtime work with stable run/submission/attempt/node/partition links; no acceptance stub masquerades as completion
acceptance.observed_result: The standard SQLModel backend stores actual runtime reports in a tenant/workspace-scoped table. Managed status reads durable worker state, and report/lineage queries return the real report after backend restart. The worker also publishes scoped start/completion events with stable run, submission, plan and attempt identities; the managed transfer recovery test observed events for both attempts after a crash following report persistence. Explicitly durable JSON outputs are persisted under hashed per-run roots; headless and HTTP downloads require the separate run.artifact.content action at run and artifact scope, use bounded SafeIoPolicy reads, and survived service restart in the application and standard SQLModel tests. Lineage queries now include stable run-to-attempt and attempt-to-executed-node edges. The report preserves both the executing attempt and the result-reconciliation attempt when a worker restarts after report publication; the focused managed application/backend and authorization suites passed 89 tests. Runtime report lineage now also links source nodes to bounded, run-scoped opaque partition IDs observed during partition-completeness checks; metadata records source key names and counts without values. Sink/output partition records now link committed sink nodes to bounded, run-scoped opaque partition IDs. Public lineage exposes produced partition nodes and key names without values. A serialized managed request reconstructs correctly from immutable mapping metadata, and the focused managed/runtime result suite passed 38 tests.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Commit-success/report-failure recovers publication without rerunning ETL; result and cleanup state truthfully represent remaining obligations
acceptance.observed_result: Worker report recovery still proves that a committed report is reused after lease expiry and restart without rerunning ETL, including status preservation after a report-write interruption. Artifact cleanup now has focused bounded-batch, filesystem-failure/retry, missing-file, symlink, run-status-preservation, and managed SQLite scope/restart coverage. The managed retention case preserves another scope and reports completed cleanup after restart. An isolated PostgreSQL report-store campaign now also proves artifact cleanup failure state, retry, retained run status, and completion metadata survive engine disposal and reopen. A persistent report-store outage campaign then committed a managed CSV sink once, recovered its hash-verified report from the SQLModel durable snapshot after backend restart, served the authorized report while the report store remained down, and reconciled publication after recovery. Changing the source between process instances left the sink output unchanged; publication state transitioned truthfully from pending to published. The focused managed backend/report/retention batch passed 59 tests.
provider_version_tuple: ETLantic workspace candidate; SQLModel durable-work snapshot backed by SQLite for outage/restart recovery

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Event resume, duplicates, cursor gaps, pagination, retention and artifact authorization pass reconnect and isolation cases
acceptance.observed_result: Event-history and SSE qualification covers reconnect via opaque cursor and Last-Event-ID, duplicate suppression, cursor gaps/expiry (410), bounded pages, run filtering, authorization, and secret redaction. Memory and SQLite tombstone tests plus isolated PostgreSQL 16.13 tests prove bounded scoped pruning, expired-key retry behavior, sequence continuity, and restart durability; PostgreSQL cursor-retention and per-scope event-count policies also passed. Owner-scope service tests compared headless and HTTP run status, event history, report, artifact listing, and artifact-content denials; a foreign owner could not see a private event marker, and authorization denied before event/report data access. Separate durable artifact tests cover per-artifact authorization, private download headers and retrieval after restart. The focused PostgreSQL, memory/SQLite retention, SSE, and owner-isolation batch passed 23 tests.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Test/catalog/schema/preflight actions run outside the gateway with action authorization, pagination, deadlines, redaction and scoped receipts
acceptance.observed_result: Durable secret-free connector action jobs execute in the fenced worker with authorization rechecks, bounded pagination/results, deadlines, cancellation, redaction and owner/environment/security-domain-scoped receipts and cursors. Foundry saved-connection handlers completed connection test, bounded schema inspection and deployment preflight through the worker against the local Semblance REST simulator. The receipts contained no token or dataset/file metadata, and the simulator recorded no transaction or upload. The focused action, scope and simulator command passed 25 tests.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Preview executes only in a qualified bounded action role, isolates credentials, limits/redacts returned data and enforces separate retention
acceptance.observed_result: Preview runs through the separately authorized, deadline-bound action worker. Foundry preview-resource resolution binds trusted owner context to one saved connection, opaque resource, exact file path and committed transaction. The public source connector rejects non-CSV or non-exact resources and enforces the file-size ceiling before download. The worker applies row/byte caps, provider-sensitive and caller-selected field redaction, truncation status and separate result retention. The Semblance-backed worker returned a one-row redacted sample, marked remaining rows truncated, disclosed no token, and performed no write; an oversized announced file was rejected before download, and bounded streaming cut off an under-reported response. The combined Foundry/action/SQLModel campaign passed 42 tests, including preview TTL cleanup and restart recovery.
provider_version_tuple: preview result TTL 60 seconds in SQLModel persistence test

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Explicit provisioning has permission, idempotency, effect and cleanup evidence; ordinary inspection does not create or mutate targets
acceptance.observed_result: Explicit provisioning and cleanup remain distinct, separately authorized actions. The typed request rejects nullable primary keys before provider I/O. The SQLAlchemy PostgreSQL action handler accepts only safe table schemas, uses create-only behavior, records owner scope/action/effect/schema fingerprint transactionally, and recovers the same effect receipt after a provider commit. A second action cannot replace that target. Cleanup checks the worker-verified successful parent and exact scope/effect binding, drops only that table, and leaves an idempotent tombstone. SQLite and isolated PostgreSQL 16.13 loopback tests passed. The PostgreSQL schema-inspection call preserved the database table set, and Semblance schema inspection performed no transaction or upload.
provider_version_tuple: Semblance==0.9.0 Foundry REST API simulator for Foundry read-only inspection

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Trusted owner/workload/scope/purpose reaches each worker/action secret and resource access; tampered references and cross-owner cache reuse are rejected
acceptance.observed_result: Server-derived principal, tenant, workspace, environment, security domain and resource owner reach managed secret providers, storage/connectors and isolated action workers. Secret cache entries are partitioned by all eight authority fields, including principal issuer/kind/subject, and unscoped callers cannot reuse managed values. Managed late-bound secret policy is rechecked before provider and cache access. Finalized input reads require the exact accepted operation lease and reject altered bytes and forged or cross-scope references. Lease IDs bind environment and principal; a managed-worker regression proved a retry accepted with the legacy lease identity recovers under current code. PostgreSQL multiprocess lease/cleanup races passed. Focused scope, secret, action, upload and Semblance Foundry simulator suites passed 88 tests plus 9 PostgreSQL resource cases.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Exact-version and authorized late-binding modes cover rotation/revocation/expiry/outage; actual version is auditable without leaking values
acceptance.observed_result: The managed secret-resolution regression campaign passed 81 tests across runtime, cache, and managed HTTP paths. Exact-version leased reads report the selected version; authorized current-alias reads bypass cache, observe rotation, and record each actual version. Lease acquisition happens after late-binding authorization, renewal runs during active execution, expiry or renewal outage cancels the run with PMEXEC405, and revocation runs on success and failure. Revocation failure records a redacted cleanup obligation and PMEXEC406. Provider exceptions and secret payloads do not appear in reports or security events. Capability/method mismatches fail closed before provider I/O. Cache tests cover scope partitioning, invalidation, immediate expiry, zero-TTL non-retention, invalid TTLs, and invalid capacity. Ruff and Pyright passed for changed source and tests.
provider_version_tuple: ETLantic workspace candidate; in-memory leased provider qualification fixture

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Finalized uploads bind immutable version/checksum/length/owner; workers reject tampering, unsafe paths and unsupported format/resource locators
acceptance.observed_result: Finalized input references bind immutable version, SHA-256, byte length, tenant, workspace and owner, without a physical storage locator. The store rejects forged digest/length/scope/owner references, cross-scope reads, unsupported media/formats and altered persisted bytes. The local files connector rejects path, URI, and storage-path injection, an external physical binding location, missing authorization resolvers, and resolver content whose length or checksum differs from the reference. Managed worker cases rejected empty, malformed, over-budget and same-length tampered CSV inputs before sink publication. PostgreSQL 16.13 multi-process lease-versus-cleanup qualification passed six forced and simultaneous trials. The selected threat, worker, and persistence command passed 37 tests.
provider_version_tuple: Python 3.14.3 clean-wheel smoke for migration 010 and leased reads

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Leases protect accepted/retry/replay inputs from retention; aborted uploads, orphans and expired inputs have bounded cleanup and stable outcomes
acceptance.observed_result: Memory and SQLModel upload stores protect accepted references with durable owner-scoped leases, allow reads past staging expiry while a lease is live, and perform bounded expiry/orphan cleanup. Abort is limited to staged uploads. The managed worker rejected the initial run before runtime startup, then executed retry, rerun and replay from the same finalized resource; four durable leases preserved reads beyond staging TTL. HTTP cleanup qualification verifies permission denial, caller-owner scoping, bounded batches, stable candidate counts and idempotent empty cleanup. The combined input-resource, CSV, HTTP, worker and migration suite passed 56 tests with no skips. PostgreSQL 16.13 multi-process lease-versus-cleanup qualification passed six trials, including both serialized orderings and four simultaneous races; no successful lease referred to deleted bytes. The clean Python 3.14.3 wheel smoke verified lease reads after backend restart.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Manual, scheduled and external triggers produce equivalent effective plans, authorization and admission for the same declared intent
acceptance.observed_result: An injected bearer-token verifier authenticated an external workload principal without a live identity provider. Manual, scheduled and external requests for the same declared intent, profile and immutable revision were admitted through ManagedApplicationService and persisted identical plan fingerprints, effective fingerprints and revision IDs. Missing/invalid credentials returned 401, authenticated but unauthorized workload returned opaque 404, and a forged X-Principal header could not override the verified identity. Rejected requests created no extra outbox item. The AC-level regression passed.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Pinned/latest-approved selection, workload identity and parameter policy are recorded once per occurrence and survive concurrent edits/restarts
acceptance.observed_result: A schedule configured for latest-approved selected the alias target at occurrence time, after the alias changed since schedule creation, and durably recorded that exact revision with the authenticated scheduler workload principal. The scheduler principal had an independent run.submit authorization grant; binding that identity to the schedule was separately authorized. A versioned parameter reference resolved into the accepted run request and its policy fingerprint, while a SecretRef was required to pin an immutable version and no secret values were persisted. After acceptance, the firing-link acknowledgement was lost and the approval alias moved back. A restarted scheduler reused the firing snapshot, recovered the same accepted run and retained the original revision and parameter/reference policy fingerprints. A SQLModel store close/reopen regression retained selection policy, workload identity, parameter/secret references and firing metadata. The managed scheduler/API campaign passed 73 tests.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: DST/timezone/misfire/catch-up/overlap/concurrency and scheduler outage cases preserve occurrence idempotency and firing-to-run linkage
acceptance.observed_result: The schedule clock and occurrence-recovery campaign passed 49 tests with one optional PostgreSQL-scope case skipped because its dedicated URL was not configured. Coverage includes timezone-normalized intervals, a New York spring-forward gap and both UTC occurrences in the fall-back repeated hour, bounded catch-up, misfire skip, overlap, effective windows, dual scheduler replicas, stale pause-after-scan claims, and scoped occurrence identity through memory and SQLite snapshot restart. A simulated wake transport outage after the firing/outbox commit recovered after process replacement with the original firing and submission and no duplicate. Scheduler drain and leadership fencing regressions also passed.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Allowed actions reflect caller/state/provider with stable reasons; commands reauthorize and enforce state preconditions despite concurrent transitions
acceptance.observed_result: Managed run actions report caller authorization, provider capability and terminal-state reasons. The 64-case managed/backend/CP1 authorization matrix passed, including authorization revocation and worker-completion races after action discovery; commands reauthorize and return the durable terminal state.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Retry/rerun/replay/resume/repair/backfill enqueue and execute qualified work, with distinct command identity, idempotency and parent/run/attempt lineage
acceptance.observed_result: A managed checkpoint-resume command validates that a checkpoint belongs to the parent submission, admits an idempotent child submission with a distinct run identity, and preserves command, checkpoint, parent-run and parent-submission references in the immutable execution envelope. The child executes a real JSON-to-CSV managed pipeline through the durable worker, persists a successful report, and records a resume parent-to-child lineage edge. Named runtime artifacts resolve in the parent run’s scoped artifact workspace. State-aware run actions advertise resume only for failed/cancelled runs with a verified envelope and no unresolved effect. Memory qualification covers worker interruption after checkpoint creation, HTTP acceptance, idempotent retry after parent state changes, missing-checkpoint rejection and unknown-effect blocking. Repair/backfill commands and their full lifecycle semantics are still unimplemented; no complete AC-level pass is asserted.
acceptance.open_reason: Managed checkpoint resume is implemented and locally qualified. Executable repair/backfill semantics, attempt lineage for the full command family and the complete lifecycle case remain pending.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Cancel, qualified pause/resume and safe amendments have tested boundaries; accepted snapshots and old attempts remain immutable
acceptance.observed_result: Memory, SQLite and PostgreSQL campaigns passed pause-after-scan, resume, stale-claim fencing, active-firing amendment rejection, stale-revision rejection and completed-firing amendment. A deterministic due-scan/pause interleaving produced no firing or outbox item; resume admitted the same occurrence. After completion, compare-and-swap amendment advanced the revision, preserved the prior firing record and rejected claims against the old revision. The HTTP amendment route requires schedule.write, accepts only the expected revision and replacement spec, and rejects stale revisions. Authorization-order and public-control coverage include the new operation; CP1 and CP-GA OpenAPI snapshots record 92 operations.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Live PostgreSQL append/upsert/replace, key/schema validation, permissions, overlaps, staged failure and commit/reconciliation cases pass
acceptance.observed_result: Isolated PostgreSQL 16.14 provider and overlap cases passed 10 tests in the combined current rerun. Coverage includes append, keyed upsert, replacement, key/schema behavior, bounded inspection, permission denial without mutation, staged rollback, lost-ack reconciliation, table-alias identity, managed overlap rejection, fail-closed unknown identities, and disjoint resource acceptance.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Foundry connector tests pass against the Semblance-backed API simulator for dataset/branch/file operations, all declared write modes, overlap, and effect/reconciliation in independently configured loopback scopes
acceptance.observed_result: The Semblance 0.9.0 simulator qualification passed 26 tests against two independent loopback scopes with distinct datasets, pinned transactions, namespaces, tokens, and seed files. Both scopes exercised append, replace, and snapshot; pinned reads, branch/file isolation, wrong-dataset and wrong-token denial, and lost-ack effect reconciliation passed. Exact source/sink file identity matches were rejected by the managed runtime before transaction creation in each scope. No live Foundry account was used.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Immutable CSV inputs exercise parsing/type/encoding choices, empty/malformed/oversize data and resource retention through the real worker
acceptance.observed_result: Directory CSV tests exercise strict typed parsing, encoding/delimiter selection, and empty/malformed/oversize rejection. Real managed-worker tests consumed typed UTF-8 BOM/semicolon immutable input past staging TTL and produced failed runs without sink effects for empty, malformed and connector-byte-over-budget finalized uploads. They also rejected a same-length stored-byte tamper after acceptance; invalid data was not exposed in reports. The combined input-resource, CSV, HTTP, worker and migration suite passed 56 tests with no skips, including six PostgreSQL 16.13 multi-process lease/cleanup trials and 19 SQLite/PostgreSQL migration cases.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: All 12 minimum source/destination pairings and advertised modes pass through the managed worker with success/failure evidence, using live PostgreSQL, immutable CSV fixtures, and two independently configured Semblance-backed Foundry scopes
acceptance.observed_result: 20 managed-worker pairing/mode cases passed against PostgreSQL 16.13 and two concurrently served, independently configured Semblance 0.9.0 scopes. The cases cover all 12 source/destination pairs and PostgreSQL append/upsert/replace modes. Every case records a successful provider effect, then a failed accepted run with stable diagnostic codes and verifies the committed destination stayed unchanged. Existing AC056-034 simulator qualification supplies independent cross-scope credential denial, overlap, pinned-read and lost-ack reconciliation evidence.
provider_version_tuple: Semblance 0.9.0; two independently configured loopback scopes

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: An independently built private provider installs without an adopter or core edit; its schema/options/native references survive authoring, submission and execution
acceptance.observed_result: The qualification script built separate core and etlantic-private-ac056037 wheels, installed both into an isolated Python 3.11.15 environment, and ran the generic consumer with workspace import paths removed. Production allowlist authorization and catalog discovery reported the installed provider schema/version; its native dataset reference and projection option were preserved by authoring, plan and durable submission, then consumed by the standard managed worker to produce the expected CSV row. The consumer supplied no connector registration or ETL loop.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Issue #150 disclosure regression and the complete multi-tenant/owner redaction campaign pass for services, HTTP, actions, events and artifacts
acceptance.observed_result: The focused managed service, HTTP, action-job, event, report, and artifact disclosure campaign passed 117 tests. Owner, tenant, workspace, environment, and security-domain variants all returned matching opaque 404s through headless and HTTP paths for run results and connector-action receipts. Denied run lookups did not open the report store, and private event markers and owner identities were absent from responses. The issue #150 explicit not_found regression also passed with existing and absent run IDs under concurrent headless/HTTP calls and no existence probes.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Real PostgreSQL control-plane persistence passes multi-process accept/race/restart/backup/restore and failure campaigns; memory/SQLite remain separately labelled
acceptance.observed_result: Isolated PostgreSQL 16.14 accepted-work persistence passed the multi-process idempotency race, independent-store restart reads, and managed retry/intent-conflict campaign. A transaction fault raised before the outbox insert and left neither an accepted submission nor an orphan receipt. A custom-format pg_dump restored into a separate database with the accepted snapshot and its single pending outbox row intact. SQLite and memory results remain separately labeled in the qualification record.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Built wheels install in a clean environment; package/export/schema/OpenAPI compatibility, migrations, version skew and upgrade/rollback behavior are recorded
acceptance.observed_result: All 25 candidate wheels built and dependency-resolved together into a fresh isolated CPython 3.11.15 environment. All 25 installed public package roots and 387 declared exports resolved from site-packages. All 24 adapter base-package constraints accepted the installed 0.55.0 core (or medallantic for SparkForge) and rejected 0.54.99 and 0.56.0. Installed CP1 and CP-GA OpenAPI 3.1 matched the committed path and operation-ID snapshots; both had 57 component schemas and 161 resolving local schema references, with matching component hashes. The installed SQLModel migration chain upgraded to 012 and completed rollback/re-upgrade from each supported CP1 head 005–011 while preserving a definition, submission identity and event history.
